Tricycle prints the tanka whole, in exactly these five lines with these line breaks, all lower case after the opening Although, and closing with a full stop: Although the wind / blows terribly here, / the moonlight also leaks / between the roof planks / of this ruined house. Its credit reads From The Ink Dark Moon: Love Poems by Ono No Komachi and Izumi Shikibu, Women of the Ancient Court of Japan, translated by Jane Hirshfield with Mariko Aratani, published by Vintage Books, translation copyright 1986 to 1990 by Jane Hirshfield. So the wording is the named translators' and no drift has crept in. Attribution: the poem is Izumi Shikibu's, not Ono no Komachi's, in the half of the book given to her; the same rendering is carried under the same first line by the Poetry Foundation. Locator: it is the entire five line tanka, untitled and known by its first line, so the complete tanka is the honest locator and nothing is cropped. Verse rule met: line breaks kept with a spaced slash, in the translators' own lineation, never run together as prose. shipped.js: not shipped, nothing near, Izumi Shikibu 0 of 3 for the year, not banned. In scope: court poetry of around the year 1000, no scripture, lyric, proverb or post-1999 work. Publishable and on theme: moonlight coming in through the broken roof is exactly holding when it is hard. Source line leads with the name, no dash, no straight double quote, 121 characters. Tag Poetry is the form. One honest limit, not enough to break it: the translation first appeared from Scribner in 1988 and the source dates it 1990, which is the Vintage printing the evidence page credits, so the year names the edition quoted rather than the first appearance.
